value.body: A maintenance planner works out what maintenance each aircraft needs and when, based on flying hours, cycles and calendar limits. They prepare work packages for hangar teams, track parts and keep technical records ready for audits. Airlines and MRO firms hire planners, mostly in office settings at bases.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: AME training or an engineering diploma / degree

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Maintenance tracking software, spreadsheets, aircraft maintenance programmes

items.label: Aircraft in passenger operation with Indian scheduled airlines
items.note: Each aircraft needs its own maintenance plan and records
items.source: Ministry of Civil Aviation, Rajya Sabha reply (as reported)

items.label: DGCA-approved AME training institutes (CAR-147 Basic)
items.source: Ministry of Civil Aviation, Parliament reply (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers with AME training often start in technical records or planning support at an airline or MRO, sometimes after time on the hangar floor. Knowledge of the aircraft maintenance programme and DGCA record-keeping rules is built on the job.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Reading maintenance programmes and task cards

value.title: At a glance
items: More office-based than hangar work, with fewer night shifts.
Next roles: senior planner, technical services, or quality and reliability roles.
Errors in records have regulatory consequences, so accuracy matters.
